resources.string: Tap or drag on the chart to read values.
How far motor and battery current may go each way. Past the absolute maximum the controller cuts out with a fault.
Current allowed at each battery voltage. Drawing current is reduced as the battery empties, regen as it fills up. Outside the input voltage range the controller stops with a fault.
Drive current is reduced as the motor nears its ERPM limit in either direction. Braking current stays available.
Current allowed as the temperature rises. Drive is cut back earlier than braking, so some braking is left. Past the end the controller stops with a fault.
Drive current is reduced close to maximum duty cycle, so the motor eases into its top speed instead of hitting it.
Extra current near maximum duty cycle that lets the motor spin faster than the battery voltage alone allows, at the cost of efficiency and heat.
Output for each input position. Below the straight line the throttle is gentler around center; above it, sharper.
Throttle for each receiver pulse length, with the deadband where small stick movements do nothing.
Output when the input jumps to full and is let go. Positive ramping time sets how fast it rises, negative ramping time how fast it falls.
Field weakening is off while its maximum current is 0 A.
No duty cycle limit while it starts at 100 %.
Regen is never reduced: its cutoff starts above the maximum input voltage.
